subject.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy

question: Should inbound debounce policy become a permanent Plugin SDK hook, or should the canonical solution remain operator-facing WhatsApp conversation configuration?
rationale: Both open proposals solve the same user need but establish conflicting long-term ownership, UX, and compatibility contracts that code review cannot safely choose.

options.title: Adopt the generic plugin hook
options.body: Choose this path if reusable plugins should own message-admission policy, then close the competing configuration path after live proof and exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Prefer conversation configuration
options.body: Choose https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970 if operators should control timing directly without a new cross-plugin hook contract.

options.title: Decline new policy surfaces
options.body: Keep the existing global and account behavior if neither proposal justifies its compatibility and maintenance cost.

recommendation.title: Adopt the generic plugin hook
recommendation.body: Choose this path if reusable plugins should own message-admission policy, then close the competing configuration path after live proof and exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest available contract-routing candidate from the prior direction discussion and adjacent hook architecture work.
